records.notes: Live CLI probes ran this round for claude-fable-5-1, claude-fable-5, fable, opus, sonnet and haiku (all exit 0); see the Capture log section in audit-2026-09.md. entries.source: `claude --model claude-fable-5-1 -p ok --output-format json`: exit 0, resolved to itself (modelUsage: claude-fable-5-1); also the Anthropic model list in the Claude Code session environment
`claude --model claude-fable-5 -p ok --output-format json`: exit 0, resolved to itself (modelUsage: claude-fable-5), so it is not an alias and is selectable on the default path

`claude --model fable -p ok --output-format json`: exit 0, resolved to claude-fable-5-1 (modelUsage), confirming `fable` floats to 5.1; also `claude --help` (claude 2.1.274) describes fable as the alias for the latest model
entries.note: Label changed from `Fable 5` to `Fable (latest)`: the alias already resolves to 5.1, and an unversioned label cannot go stale. The id is unchanged so stored selections keep resolving.

entries.source: `claude --model sonnet -p ok --output-format json`: exit 0, resolved to claude-sonnet-5 (modelUsage); alias floating not established by a single resolution
`claude --model opus -p ok --output-format json`: exit 0, resolved to claude-opus-5 (modelUsage); alias floating not established by a single resolution

`claude --help` (claude 2.1.274) on the dev box, 2026-09-27: --model takes an alias (fable, opus, sonnet) or a model's full name; Claude Opus 5.5's full model name is `claude-opus-5-5`, and a Claude Code session on the same box runs as exactly that model id. `opus-5.5` is not an alias the CLI documents. Reasoning ladder mirrors the other Opus/Sonnet/Fable entries in this block (low/medium/high/xhigh/max via --max-thinking-tokens). Live run 2026-09-27 (`claude -p ... --model claude-opus-5-5 --max-thinking-tokens 1024`) on claude 2.1.274 was refused with API error 400 claude_code_version_too_old: "version 2.1.280 or newer is required", so the id is recognised but needs Claude Code 2.1.280+. The same call on claude 2.1.283 answered, with modelUsage reporting claude-opus-5-5. The dev box's global install was updated to 2.1.283 the same day, and the call through it answered too.

`claude --model haiku -p ok --output-format json`: exit 0, resolved to the dated id claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (modelUsage), unlike the other three which resolve to undated ids; alias floating not established by a single resolution

evidence.authContext: ChatGPT sign-in via `codex login`; live CLI capture on the dev box (`codex debug models`) enumerates the GPT-6 family entries directly
evidence.source: `codex debug models` output on the dev box, 2026-09-29: codex 0.155.0 and later offers all three GPT-6 models: gpt-6-astra and gpt-6-sol (levels low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra; default low) and gpt-6-luna (levels low, medium, high, xhigh, max; default medium), all with the fast tier. The repository's prior "gpt-6-astra is the only GPT-6 model" record came from codex 0.154.0 and is superseded by this capture; the dev box's Codex is now 0.159.0. There is no plain gpt-6 in Codex's own catalogue.

records.notes: First manifest record for codex-cli. Adds gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna with live-captured evidence; every other pre-existing seeded base id is recorded unverified pending a live `codex --model <id>` capture so no seeded id is left without a manifest entry.

entries.source: `codex debug models` output (codex 0.154.0) on the dev box, 2026-09-27: gpt-6-astra listed with default effort low and supported efforts low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. The same output also lists `additional_speed_tiers: ["fast"]` for gpt-6-astra (service tier `priority`, named "Fast": 2x speed, increased usage), the same fast tier documented for gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna and gpt-5.5, which establishes supportsFast: true for gpt-6-astra in CODEX_MODEL_CAPABILITIES. Live run 2026-09-27: `codex exec --json -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort="low"` completed and answered.

`codex debug models` output (codex 0.159.0) on the dev box, 2026-09-29: gpt-6-sol listed with default effort low and supported efforts low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra, plus `additional_speed_tiers: ["fast"]` (service tier `priority`), the same ladder and fast tier as gpt-6-astra. Live run 2026-09-29: `codex exec` answered on gpt-6-sol.

`codex debug models` output (codex 0.159.0) on the dev box, 2026-09-29: gpt-6-luna listed with default effort medium and supported efforts low, medium, high, xhigh, max, plus `additional_speed_tiers: ["fast"]` (service tier `priority`). Live run 2026-09-29: `codex exec` answered on gpt-6-luna.
